_what: Hand-authored pipeline INPUT. Not an edit of any pipeline output — src/data/dex.json stays wholly produced by a run, and a re-run against unchanged inputs still reproduces it byte for byte.
_why: Five Mega forms exist in the PokeAPI exports (base stats, sprites, form names) but their abilities have no upstream source at all. Three are the Z Megas (absol-mega-z, garchomp-mega-z, lucario-mega-z); two are the 1.2.0 Megas (golisopod-mega, baxcalibur-mega), released by the game before the exports caught up. This file supplies exactly those abilities and nothing else. Base stats and sprite paths keep coming from PokeAPI for these forms like every other, and every roster entry now comes from the roster page.
_delete_when: An upstream source starts carrying a field below. Delete that entry, re-run the pipeline, and the dataset must come out unchanged. When every entry is gone, delete this file and the two hooks that read it.
_added_note: Empty: the roster page now carries a released row for every form this file used to supply one for (Mega Absol Z, Mega Garchomp Z, Mega Lucario Z, all 1.2.0). The types it recorded for them matched what upstream published, so their deletion left the dataset unchanged. parse.py fails rather than let a row here shadow a released one.
_abilities_note: Rows that pokemon_abilities.csv would carry if PokeAPI had them. Same shape as that file: pokemon_id keyed, each slot naming an ability_id and whether it is hidden.

_new_abilities_note: An ability PokeAPI does not have at all, so it needs the rows abilities.csv, ability_names.csv and ability_flavor_text.csv would carry. The id is far outside the upstream range (max upstream id is 10060) so it can never collide with a real one, and so that its being synthetic is visible at a glance.
